status: traced 2026-09-30 from land_8k_16_annotated_rift.png at outline threshold 6; boxes and spans are measured, nothing is built, nothing installed, not seen in game
rung: datapack plus functions and commands (CLAUDE.md principle 6, rungs 5 and 6). Cobblemon native has no player-zone concept; no installed addon gates an area; Cobbleverse ships none; no config key expresses a box a player may not stand in. A vanilla datapack does: a minecraft:location advancement fires on a player inside a box and its reward function acts. tools/gulch_mine.py already runs exactly this shape for the gulch (data/gulch_mine.json zone, gate), so the rung is proven here rather than assumed.
y_why: full height, as RIFT_ZONES.md section 4 draws a zone: flying over, digging under or pearling in all end with the player inside the boxes, so the test catches every route in. The same numbers data/gulch_mine.json zone.y uses.
grid_why: the boxes are rasterised on an 8-block grid and merged into maximal rectangles. 8 is the grid data/legendaries.json's spawn-free zones and the route corridor boxes already share, so a zone edge lands where other authored edges land. Finer than the 32 RIFT_ZONES.md section 4 assumed, and still a few hundred boxes: the cost is one location test per zone per second per player.

source.where: the source root beside the heightmap; not in the repo, pinned by sha256 in data/rift_regions.json
source.how: each zone is the union of whole regions flood-filled from data/rift_regions.json's seeds, exactly as that file describes its own regions, optionally split by one cut line
source.why: the eleven regions are the owner's own traced partition of the Rift, drawn by hand on the heightmap at 1 pixel = 1 block. A zone built from them has the strongest provenance available and needs no new tracing. tools/rift_zones.py trace re-derives them and refuses to go on unless every region's flood fill reproduces data/rift_regions.json's recorded bbox exactly.
source.not_the_lip_ring: data/gulch_mine.json traces its zone from derived/rift_sculpt/plan.json, the sculpted lip ring. That file is a derived input and is refused to an isolated agent (CLAUDE.md, 'Launching a writing agent' step 3), so these zones are not traced from it. They do not need to be: the traced regions already tile the Rift's interior and their shared edges are where the owner put them. See RIFT_ZONES_BUILD.md 'What was not traced'.

pass.why: one scoreboard objective per zone, cob_pass_z1 .. cob_pass_z5, set to 1 by the zone's guard when the player qualifies and never unset (RIFT_ZONES.md section 4). Per player, so multiplayer needs nothing extra: each player is judged on their own score and a qualified player cannot carry an unqualified one through.
pass.fail_closed: the score is NOT tested inside the advancement. RIFT_ZONES.md section 4 puts a minecraft:entity_scores condition with cob_pass below 1 in the in_zone advancement; that fails OPEN, because minecraft:entity_scores does not match when the objective has no value for that player, which is every player who has never been given one. So the advancement tests location alone and the reward function tests the score with `execute unless score @s <obj> matches 1..`, which is true for an unset score. A player with no score is turned back; a player with 1 is let be.
pass.grant: the guard's dialogue calls `function cobblers:rift_zones/<z>/grant` rather than composing a scoreboard command of its own, so the objective name lives in one place and Codex's dialogue does not have to know it.
pass.qualify: each zone also emits `function cobblers:rift_zones/<z>/qualify`, which grants the pass only if the player actually meets the zone's threshold, read server-side from the badge advancements. Dialogue may call `grant` (it has already checked) or `qualify` (let the server check). The caught-count zones have no server-side qualify: see zones.z4.qualify_why.

exempt_why: creative and spectator are never turned back, as data/gulch_mine.json's gate does it: an operator inspecting a zone must not be bounced out of it.

gatehouse.knock_why: the two walkway blocks directly OUTSIDE the guard, under the gatehouse's own roof, where a player stands face to face with it. This box is what calls the zone's qualify: a minecraft:location advancement over it, exactly as data/gulch_mine.json gate.knock does at the gulch's grille, whose reward function runs cobblers:rift_zones/<zone>/qualify. gatehouse.why: docs/mechanics/RIFT_ZONES.md section 6, its drawn section, unchanged: a one-wide walkway between obsidian, roofed at y+2 so nothing jumps the guard, closed by a two-high barrier column directly behind the guard. The barrier is what physically stops a player; the guard reads as the thing that stops them. The passed player arrives 3 blocks inside facing in; an unqualified player is put 8 blocks outside facing away; the exit box sits 5 blocks inside on the walkway.
gatehouse.not_built_here: the guard NPCs themselves. tools/rift_zones.py places an armour stand placeholder at each guard's block, exactly as data/rift_sculpt.json entrance_policy does for its five trailheads: 'Guards' trailheads are marked with an armour stand placeholder and not staffed; Codex writes them'.

wall.rise_why: docs/mechanics/RIFT_ZONES.md section 5's recommendation: sixteen blocks cannot be walked or jumped, so the wall closes what it crosses. The cross-wall rows in that section's table run floor to rim+16; this file keeps rim+16 and takes the rim from the heightmap per column rather than from one number, so the wall follows the ground it crosses.
wall.palette_why: docs/mechanics/RIFT_ZONES.md section 5 names exactly these: obsidian, crying obsidian, blackstone, gilded blackstone, purple and magenta stained glass and panes, tinted glass. No minecraft:nether_portal block anywhere: portal blocks teleport players. Obsidian also cannot be moved by pistons. tools/rift_zones.py report checks every one of them against data/spawn_blocks.json and fails if any is a block a spawn condition names.
wall.superseded: the rim wall and the 257 spires of RIFT_ZONES.md section 5 are NOT built. RIFT_FRACTURE.md supersedes them: 'the scarps are the barrier'. Only the cross-walls at the three cuts and their gatehouses are generated here, about 71,000 blocks instead of about 789,000.
wall.frontier_reach_why: the maximum the tool may grow one zone's traced mask to find its frontier with the next. It searches upward from 2 and records the smallest reach that works as frontier_reach_used, so the number in the data is measured, not chosen. The owner's annotation draws each region's outline in black BETWEEN two regions and leaves unclaimed ground in places, so two traced masks never touch.
wall.core_why: 2 thick, as docs/mechanics/RIFT_ZONES.md section 5's cross-wall rows are. The frontier is already a band a few columns wide where the boundary runs diagonally, so the core is applied along the frontier's own columns rather than normal to a straight line.
wall.floor_band_why: a frontier column carries a wall only where it crosses walkable floor: ground within 15 of the floor at the cut's `through` point. The Rift's floor is y82-89 and its rim y87-149 (docs/mechanics/RIFT_ZONES.md section 1), so 15 separates the floor from the scarp at every one of the three frontiers. Above it no wall is generated, because docs/mechanics/RIFT_FRACTURE.md supersedes the rim wall: 'the scarps are the barrier'. Measured on the canonical heightmap via tools/ground.py.

driver.why: the zone check is advancement-driven and needs no tick driver at all, exactly as data/gulch_mine.json's does (tools/reapply.py's step table says of the gulch 'the gate, the zone check ... act on their own and need no step'). The pack's only tick work is the one-line objective creation on load. This key records that deliberate absence so a later reader does not add a driver to a system that does not want one.

hoopa_cradle.question: docs/story/FACTION.md says (3297, 2603); data/rift_regions.json sites it under the relic area at (3357, 3306).
hoopa_cradle.why: three independent checks, 2026-09-30. (1) (3297, 2603) is OUTSIDE the Rift: an even-odd test against data/landmarks.json rift.extent.polygons[0] puts it outside the outline, and its ground is y118 on the canonical heightmap, at the rim's median height (y121), not on a floor of y82-89. (2) It is not under the relic area: relic_area_shrine's traced bbox is 3285-3429 x 3229-3384, and z2603 is 626 blocks north of it. (3) (3357, 3306) is inside the extent, inside relic_area_shrine, has ground y88 (so the recorded 76 blocks of cover over a floor at y12 is right), and is bracketed by data/deep_city.json's reserved volume 3317,-12,3266 - 3397,72,3346. rift_regions, deep_city and the heightmap agree; FACTION.md is the lone outlier and should be corrected to (3357, 3306).
hoopa_cradle.zone_consequence: the cradle is in Z2, which is what RIFT_ZONES.md section 2a requires. It is only in Z2 because this file moved the throat cut west to x3308; at RIFT_ZONES.md's throat line (x3384-3406) the cradle would have sat in Z1 at two badges, breaking section 2a. See cuts[throat].supersedes.
hoopa_cradle.not_changed: docs/story/FACTION.md is not edited here: it is story, and correcting a coordinate in it is Codex's or the owner's. Reported instead.

registeel_region.question: which part of the Rift holds Registeel's sealed chamber; the main session recommended upper_rift (4195, 3896).
registeel_region.answer: the zone system does NOT settle the region, and says so. It settles the gate.
registeel_region.why: all three candidate columns in data/legendaries.json fall inside Z2: upper_rift (4195, 3896), rift_wilds (4288, 4204) and the_sink (3573, 3687) are in the traced upper_rift, rift_wilds and the_sink regions, every one of which is a Z2 region. So the zone system is region-neutral between them and cannot choose; the choice stays what data/legendaries.json calls it, 'owner_decision: which part of the Rift', and story (docs/story/ARC.md).
registeel_region.what_it_does_settle: Registeel's effective gate is EIGHT badges, not seven, wherever in the Rift it goes. data/legendaries.json registeel.gate is flags [gym7_cleared], status 'PROPOSED, NOT DECIDED'. Z2's pass is eight badges, so a player at seven badges cannot stand anywhere in the Rift's floor to reach it. Either the record's gate rises to gym8_cleared, or the chamber leaves the Rift. This is a real contradiction between two authored files and it does not depend on which candidate is picked.
registeel_region.not_changed: data/legendaries.json is not edited here: a legendary's gate is encounter balance, trainer-balance-designer's file, and changing it would also move the level basis (55, '5 below the provisional 7-badge cap of 64'). Reported instead.

league_opens_too_early.question: docs/STATE.md: 'the defined Rift-to-League handoff has no setter while the League opens too early on gym8_cleared'.
league_opens_too_early.answer: settled by adding z5, the League's precinct, as its own zone gated on rift_crisis_resolved.
league_opens_too_early.why: the fault is that data/progression.json's league node is unlocked_by [gym8_cleared] alone, so the League opens the moment the eighth badge is won, before the Rift's finale. Z2 cannot carry the fix: RIFT_ZONES.md section 2a puts the finale INSIDE Z2 (the cradle is on the trunk), so requiring rift_crisis_resolved to enter Z2 would be circular, a player needing to be inside the zone to earn the thing that lets them in. A second, smaller zone around the League's precinct is not circular: the player passes Z2 at eight badges, walks Victory Road, reaches the cradle, releases Hoopa, and only then G5 opens the gate. The geography for it is already traced: data/rift_regions.json's `gate` region exists precisely because of owner_intent[2], 'The entrance to the Elite Four is sealed off unless you go through the town first.'
league_opens_too_early.still_needed: the flag and its setter. See zones.z5.needs_progression: data/progression.json must gain cobblers:flag/rift_crisis_resolved and the league node must require it, and the setter is the finale's quest stage, which is Codex's story data. tools/rift_zones.py report fails until the flag exists, so the half-built state is loud rather than quiet.

multiplayer.state: per player. Each pass is a scoreboard score on the player's own name; each in_zone advancement is granted and revoked per player.
multiplayer.joins_late: nothing to catch up. A player who joins after the walls are built is tested the first time the location trigger fires, within a second of login, and is turned back if they lack the pass.
multiplayer.dies_inside: the reward function removes a spawn point set inside a zone before it turns the player back (RIFT_ZONES.md section 4), so a respawn cannot loop.
multiplayer.disconnects_inside: logging back in inside a zone fires the location test within a second, as login does.
multiplayer.different_order: the zones do not assume an order. A player may hold z4's pass and not z2's; each zone is judged alone.
multiplayer.cannot_carry: a qualified player cannot bring an unqualified one through: the guard's teleport moves only the player who talked, and the second player is turned back by the zone check.
multiplayer.mount: the reward function teleports the vehicle first (`execute on vehicle run tp @s ...`), then the player, as data/gulch_mine.json's turn_back does. Whether Cobblemon's riding survives that is UNPROVEN (RIFT_ZONES.md section 4).

unproven: every line of this file. Nothing has been installed, run on a server or seen by a player.
the caught-count call form for G4 (RIFT_ZONES.md section 3: the key is VERIFIED in the 1.8.0 source, the call form is ASSUMED, and which acquisitions move it is untested).
the guard experiment of RIFT_ZONES.md section 6: barrier behind the NPC, sprint-jump, piston, ender pearl, ridden flying Pokemon, exact teleport landing.
that a player on a ridden Pokemon is moved by `execute on vehicle run tp`.

the knock box itself: that a minecraft:location advancement over the two walkway blocks in front of the guard fires reliably on a standing player, that its reward's teleport lands where grant says, and that the `unless entity @s[x=..,dx=..]` exemption in the zone check covers exactly the same blocks. Nothing has been run.

that a player cannot reach a knock box from INSIDE its zone and use it as a free pass. The gatehouse is one wide, roofed, walled in obsidian and closed by a barrier behind the guard, so on paper the box is reachable only from outside; that is the guard experiment of RIFT_ZONES.md section 6, unrun.

that G2 reads as a gate at all now that it stands on open ground. At (3738, 5082) its one-wide walkway sat in the sculpted switchback, where the cut rim was the only walkable way past it. At the trailhead (3548, 5322) the heightmap is flat y111 for at least three columns either side, so a player can simply walk round the gatehouse. That does not break the GATE -- enforcement is the zone's own location advancement over the full height of 261 boxes, which begin 53 blocks further on, and a player who walks round is turned back to (3546.5, 112, 5330.5), 8 blocks outside the gatehouse's door, facing away. It is the READING that is unproven: whether the warden looks like something that stops you, or like a hut beside a road. The shell's obsidian wings may need widening, or the sculpt may need a parapet either side of the ramp -- both are judgement calls on built ground, and neither is measurable from here.

measured_defects.found: 2026-10-01, while moving G2 to the trailhead (guard.supersedes). NOT caused by that move.
measured_defects.what: every one of the six gatehouse shells tools/rift_zones.py build emits has a walkway a player cannot walk along. Parsed out of build/datapacks/cobblers_rift_zones and flood-filled with Minecraft's own diagonal rule -- a diagonal step is blocked when both orthogonal corners are solid -- the standable columns of G2's shell fall into FOUR disconnected pieces: [(3547, 5324)], [(3548, 5322), (3548, 5323)], [(3549, 5317) .. (3549, 5320)], [(3550, 5316)]. Only one of those breaks is the two-high barrier at (3548, 5321), which is meant to be there.
measured_defects.why: cmd_build lays the shell by stepping the walkway's centre along a unit axis and walling the two columns perpendicular to it, with the perpendicular snapped to whichever of x or z the axis leans on (`px, pz = (0, 1) if abs(dx) > abs(dz) else (1, 0)`). On a diagonal axis the centre shifts one block sideways every few steps, and the wall column of one step lands on the diagonal corner of the next, so each sideways shift seals itself.
measured_defects.scope: all six, measured: gatehouse_z1 2 of 7 columns reachable, gatehouse_z2 1 of 8, z2/victory_road_descent 1 of 8, z2/rim_post_descent 1 of 7, z2/wilds_slip 3 of 8. The two axis-aligned gates, z4 (5 of 8) and z5 (3 of 8), break ONLY at their barrier and are correct.
measured_defects.not_from_the_move: gatehouse_z2_victory_road_descent reproduces the pre-2026-10-01 G2 shell block for block -- same block, same axis, same numbers -- and splits into four pieces of the same shape. The trailhead's axis is steeper and the count is identical: 1 of 8 before, 1 of 8 after.
measured_defects.how_bad: passing the gate still works, because passing is a teleport and not a walk: the knock box's outer column is open to the road, and grant teleports the player to `arrive` past the barrier. What does NOT work is leaving on foot -- a player walking out of the Rift reaches the walkway's inner mouth and cannot step to the `exit` box one diagonal away -- and the gate reads as a wall with a hole rather than a door.
measured_defects.not_fixed_here: the fix is in cmd_build's shell geometry and it moves blocks at all six gates, which is a different change from moving one gate, needs a test of its own, and should not ride along inside this one. Whoever takes it: the walkway wants the union of the perpendicular pair at each step AND the corner columns the diagonal needs, or a Bresenham walkway with the wall laid as the complement of the walked set. The check that catches it is the flood fill above, over the emitted function, which is independent of the geometry that writes it.
measured_defects.fixed: 2026-10-01, decision B12, in tools/rift_zones.py. walkway_path() gives every diagonal step the column that joins its two ends, so the walked set is 4-connected; walkway_shell() lays the walls as the COMPLEMENT of that set instead of a perpendicular pair per step, so no wall can land on the column a bend needs; the barrier is the walkway's own next column inward of the guard rather than round(guard + inward), which on a diagonal step is a different column; and the cross-wall's `keep` set is the walkway's own columns instead of an axis cross of radius 2, which on a diagonal axis missed most of the walkway and sealed it a second time.
measured_defects.fixed_measured: re-flood-filled over the emitted functions by `python tools/rift_zones.py walkable`: all SEVEN gatehouses now come out in exactly 2 pieces, and in 1 piece with the barrier blocks opened, so the barrier is the only break. Standable columns before -> after: z1 7 -> 11 (4 pieces -> 2), z2 8 -> 11 (4 -> 2), z2/victory_road_descent 8 -> 11 (4 -> 2), z2/rim_post_descent 7 -> 11 (5 -> 2), z2/wilds_slip 8 -> 9 (3 -> 2), z4 8 -> 8 (2 -> 2), z5 8 -> 8 (2 -> 2). Not a widening: every walkway column still has at most 2 walkway neighbours (a 1-wide corridor, measured), walkway_path() raises on any 2x2 of walkway columns, and the growth is only the corner columns -- 3, 3, 3, 3, 1, 0, 0 across the seven. The two axis-aligned gates z4 and z5 are block-for-block IDENTICAL to the old output, which is the check that the change moves blocks only where the axis is diagonal.
measured_defects.note: the record says six gatehouses; there are seven (z1, z2, z2's three posts, z4, z5) and five of them were broken. The `scope` line above names all seven correctly and only its own count of six is wrong.

measured_defects.found: 2026-10-01, while fixing gatehouse_walkway_is_not_continuous (decision B12). A SEPARATE defect, not caused by that fix and not fixed by it.
measured_defects.what: `arrive` and `exit` take their y from tools/ground.py at their OWN column, g(x, z) + 1, while the gatehouse lays its walkway flat at the GUARD's feet level, g(guard) + 1, for every column of its length. Where the ground slopes along the walkway the two disagree, and then the exit box floats above the walkway's air or is buried under its floor. Measured over the emitted functions after the B12 fix: z2/victory_road_descent walkway floor y87, arrive and exit boxes at y88 (1 too high); z2/wilds_slip walkway floor y95, arrive y93 (2 too low) and exit y97 (2 too high). The other five agree exactly.
measured_defects.second_part: z5's `arrive` (3587, 2680) and `exit` (3589, 2680) are not on its gatehouse at all: its walkway runs (3571, 2680) to (3579, 2680). An inside-sited gate anchors its places on `zone_begins_at` and not on the guard's block (tools/rift_zones.py survey), and for z5 that anchor is 11 blocks along the axis, so the places land 8 blocks past the inner mouth on open ground. z4's anchor is 0 blocks along, so z4 is unaffected.
measured_defects.how_bad: a minecraft:location advancement over a box the player's feet never occupy never fires, so at those two posts the exit box cannot be stepped into even though the walkway is now continuous; and the arrival teleport puts the player 2 blocks under or over the walkway floor. UNVERIFIED in game -- this is read off the emitted commands, not observed.
measured_defects.not_fixed_here: the fix is in `trace`'s survey(), which would re-derive every place in this file and needs the annotated source map; B12's brief is the walkway's shape and says not to ride other changes along, which is the same reason the walkway fix did not ride along inside the G2 move. Whoever takes it: the places of a gate want the gatehouse's own flat floor level, g(guard) + 1, for every column the gatehouse covers, and an inside-sited gate's anchor wants to be the guard's block for anything that has to land on the walkway.

interior.why: the ground the zones must tile. Every column of it belongs to exactly one zone.
